turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Eileen? In you come. I did your observations outside, and I'll read them once you're settled.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hello Eileen, Dr Brennan. Have a seat there. What's been going on with you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah doctor, I'm a holy show. My niece's wedding in Athlone on Saturday, the band from Donegal were mighty, and then Sunday I lived in the loo.

[SEG0004] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'm Maeve, her carer, I come in every morning. She rang me Sunday in bits — diarrhoea and vomiting since that wedding, and her cousin and two others off the same table have it too.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it start for you, Eileen — Saturday night, or Sunday?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): The starter was prawns, I had the salmon after, and the cake was lemon with little flowers. The speeches went on a fierce long time, and my feet were killing me.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll get to the menu in a minute. When did you first actually get sick?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Sunday morning, early, in the hotel. I vomited before breakfast, and the diarrhoea came the same morning. Today's Wednesday, so that's three days.
[SEG0009] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Four vomits on Sunday, two on Monday, and nothing since Monday evening. The one in the car on the way home was already counted in the Sunday four.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the diarrhoea — how many times are we talking?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): A good few. Six, maybe eight, I lost count entirely. I couldn't tell you if that was one desperate day or spread over the three days.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool, or black stool?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Nuala, the cousin, she had the beef and she's laid up in Cork. She sent me a photo of the centrepieces in the middle of it, can you believe that.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leave the flowers a minute. Was there blood, or was it black?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No blood at all. Watery, brown water, like. Nothing black.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any crampy pain along with it?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit of cramp, low down in the tummy. It comes and goes, and it's easier once I've been. Not agony, mind.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you feel feverish, or have shivers?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): I was a small bit shivery on Sunday night. I don't think I had a temperature. Mostly I'm just wrecked, no energy in me.
[SEG0020] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The thermometer was normal on Monday and again this morning. She's weak, though, and her mouth is dry.
[SEG0021] person_1 (NURSE): Just now, temperature thirty-six point nine, pulse ninety-eight, blood pressure one hundred and twenty-two over seventy-eight.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grand. What have you managed to drink?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Tea, Barry's, a drop of milk. I can't look at food. Bruno the dog is eating rings around me — Maeve gave him the tin.
[SEG0024] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Two small cups of tea since yesterday and a few sips of water, that's all. Her lips are dry. I told her tea isn't proper fluid.

[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look at you. Your tongue is dry, and the skin on the back of your hand is a little slow to spring back. That's mild dehydration, not severe. Your tummy is soft, tender across the lower part, no guarding and no rigidity.

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thinking it through, this fits acute gastroenteritis from that wedding meal, with the dryness on top. Several of you sick after the same sitting, so I'd blame the food. I can't tell virus from bacteria from the chair.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking just now?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): I went to the chemist Sunday evening and bought Imodium. I've been taking it, even though Maeve was giving out yards.
[SEG0029] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I told her not to. If there's a bug you don't bung yourself up, but she did it anyway. Her blood pressure tablet is amlodipine, five milligrams by mouth every morning.
[SEG0030] person_1 (NURSE): The box she handed me says loperamide two milligrams, one capsule after each loose stool.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): That's not what I did. I took two capsules every time, so four milligrams. Since Sunday night I've been doing that.
[SEG0032] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Each capsule is two milligrams and she swallows two of them by mouth. I wouldn't like to pick which number is the real dose.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies, to medicines or to food?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): No, no allergies. I eat everything going. The prawns didn't sit right, but that's not an allergy — other people had them too.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other regular tablets besides the amlodipine and the Imodium?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): No, that's the lot. I was going to start a vitamin after Christmas and I never got round to it. The jar is still in the press.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the amlodipine — that's for your high blood pressure? Five milligrams every morning?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): It is, yeah, years now. Five milligrams every morning, and I don't miss it.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): The loperamide does slow the bowel, but with a bug I'd rather you let it out. Stop the Imodium from today. It can keep the illness going longer.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): I thought I was being sensible, and the chemist didn't stop me. Grand, I'll knock it on the head.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fluids are the bit that matters. Little sips, often, not a big glass in one go. Get Dioralyte or another rehydration sachet from the chemist, make it up as the packet says, and ease off the tea.
[SEG0042] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll collect the sachets on the way. She lives on her own, so I'll come back this evening as well as the morning and sit with her while she drinks.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Will I make the christening on Sunday week? My sister will have my life if I cry off. The neighbour says Bruno howls if I'm gone too long.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't promise the christening. If you're not keeping fluids down, if you go properly dizzy, or if you see blood, don't wait — come back here or go to the emergency department the same day.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it's not settling in three days, come back and see me. If it hasn't eased by then, we can send a stool sample, but I won't send one today.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): A stool sample, God help us. The drive home from Athlone was worse — the M6 was a pure car park the whole way.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): I won't give you a sample pot today. If Dr Brennan wants it later in the week, reception can sort the bottle.
[SEG0048] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll write the bowel movements down properly, not the six-or-eight guess, and I'll mind the sips.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): That'll help. A pulse of ninety-eight fits with being a bit dry, and most of these settle once the fluid is in and the loperamide is stopped.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): Is ninety-eight desperate? I do go a bit light when I stand up. I didn't faint or anything, I just have to catch the chair.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): That light feeling goes with the dryness. Stand up in stages, no rushing. If you actually faint, that's a same-day review, not something to sleep on.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Ye're very good. I'll stop the Imodium, I'll sip the sachets, and I'll tell the Donegal band it wasn't their doing.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Go easy. Maeve has the plan. If you slide tonight, don't sit at home hoping.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

bad.reason: Fever absent is supported by caregiver, but not specifically temporality current.

omissions.text: Loperamide dose instructions on the box were '2 mg, 1 capsule after each loose stool', but the patient says she has actually been taking 2 capsules each time (4 mg after each loose stool) since Sunday night.
No other regular tablets besides amlodipine and loperamide.
Diarrhoea described as watery brown stool.
Vomiting occurred before breakfast on Sunday.
Patient had poor appetite/could not face food.
Mild dehydration was specifically stated as 'not severe'.
Doctor advised to get Dioralyte or another rehydration sachet from the chemist and make it up as directed.
Doctor said no stool sample would be sent today, and nurse said no sample pot would be given today; reception could provide one later if needed.
